entries.why: Units 4-5 are chemistry's own S2 numbering, distinct from maths's 5-8 (see EXPECTED_UNITS in extract_book_figures.py). Titles match the curriculum word for word; lessons 4/2 and 5/2 print in the book but yielded no figures that survived review (their only crops were a section-heading callout and a lesson-review page, not diagrams).

This book prints no `الوحدة` running header or top-band opener — extract_book_figures.py's outline() only found the unit boundary via its lesson-number-restart fallback (added alongside this book), so unit here is inferred from where the book's own `الدرسُ` count drops back to 1, not read directly off the page. Lessons 1/1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/5, 2/2, 2/5 print in the book but yielded no figures that survived review — every crop under them was a decorative divider, callout, or exercise-text fragment, not a diagram.

Both G9 books number units 1-8 across the year the same way G10 maths does (S1=1-4, S2=5-8), and every one of the 28 lesson titles the book states matches the curriculum's own title exactly, unlike G10 maths's unit-1 offset (see EXPECTED_UNITS['grade-9-math'] in extract_book_figures.py). Titles the extractor could not read (u7_l3, u8_l1, u8_l3) are still placed by position: each sits between two lessons whose titles DID match, with no unaccounted-for lesson number in between.

entries.why: UNIT NUMBERS ARE OFFSET BY 2 HERE, and the offset is the entry, not a bug to correct upstream. This book prints no «الوحدة N» running header, so `outline` counts opener resets inside the one PDF and calls its units 1 and 2; the curriculum numbers them 3 and 4 across the year. Verified before it was written down: all eight of unit 3's lesson titles land exactly on the opener page `outline` detected. Same shape as the English S2 offset.

Offset by 3, same as its Grade 10 sibling. ONE figure survived review out of 14 crops — this book's maps and photographs are rasters the vector extractor cannot seed on, so all it found was drawn page furniture. It is wired for that single Asia map; the rest of the book needs the raster pipeline (`extract_book_photos.py`), not another run of this one.

Grade 8's first book of any kind, added 2026-09-12. Nine of its ten lesson titles land exactly on the opener page `outline` detected; the tenth («تركيب الذرّة والتوزيع الإلكترونيّ») is a long title whose RTL extraction breaks a substring match, not a disagreement. Its SEMESTER 2 book is absent on purpose: only two pages in it carry «الدرس» as text and both are the contents spread, so `outline` returns nothing and every crop would be unplaced.

Grade 8 maths, added 2026-09-13. Both books needed a new `OPENER_PROFILES` entry and it took two tries: the sizes alone got 15 of 17 openers in S1 and 14 of 20 in S2, because a handful of pages emit «الدرس» FUSED to the title in one span («الدرسُالنسبةُ المئويّة»), which an equality test cannot see. `dars_prefix` fixes that and both books now detect their catalog counts exactly. Worth knowing why that mattered: a missed opener does not leave a gap, it extends the PREVIOUS lesson over the missing one's pages and files its figures under the wrong lesson.

unitNumbering: The curriculum's `u{n}_l{m}` matches the number the book PRINTS in every unit except unit 1, where the book has an extra opening lesson («حل معادلات خاصة») and the rest shift by one. Units 1-4 are semester 1 and units 5-8 are semester 2, so the printed unit number also identifies which student book a figure came from — `check_semester` in scripts/extract_book_figures.py enforces that. Note the maths PDFs in attached_assets are named backwards: the file called `1st_semester` is the second-semester book. Source ids follow the books' contents, not their filenames.
